title: MarkMyWords GS answer rubric
disclaimer: This is MarkMyWords' own exam-aligned framework. UPSC does not publish a criterion-wise rubric. It has not yet been calibrated against human expert evaluators.
changelog: 0.1.0 — initial draft criteria and band descriptors. Status: calibrating (no calibration report attached).

criteria.name: Question demand & directive
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Judge whether every part of the question is addressed and whether the answer performs the moves the directive requires (e.g. 'critically analyse' needs both sides and a judgement). Do not reward length.

bands.descriptor: Does not engage with what the question asks.
Addresses the topic but misses most parts or misreads the directive.
Addresses some parts; directive partly followed.
Addresses all parts; directive followed with minor gaps.
Addresses every part with balanced depth and fully performs the directive.

criteria.name: Content & dimensions
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Judge relevance and the range of dimensions that matter for THIS question (constitutional, legal, economic, social, environmental, international, governance, technological, security). A checklist dump of irrelevant dimensions is not a strength.

bands.descriptor: Largely irrelevant or absent content.
One relevant dimension, thinly covered.
Two relevant dimensions; important ones missing.
Most relevant dimensions covered with reasonable depth.
Relevant dimensions covered with depth and selectivity.

criteria.name: Analysis & reasoning
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Reward explanation of mechanisms (how and why), trade-offs, conditions under which claims hold, and a reasoned judgement. Assertions without reasoning are not analysis.

bands.descriptor: Pure assertion; no reasoning.
States outcomes without explaining how they arise.
Some causal reasoning; one-sided or no judgement.
Clear mechanisms and both sides; judgement present but thinly argued.
common_failures: judgement not tied to the analysis

bands.descriptor: Mechanisms, trade-offs and conditions explained; judgement follows from the analysis.

criteria.name: Evidence & accuracy
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Reward accurate, relevant Articles, Acts, judgments, reports, data, schemes and examples. A factual error affects this criterion only and must be cited from the provided sources; otherwise mark it unverifiable.

bands.descriptor: No substantiation, or substantiation that is wrong.
Generic examples only, or a significant factual error.
Some specific evidence; gaps or minor inaccuracies.
Specific, accurate evidence for most claims.
Precise, accurate, well-chosen evidence supporting the key claims.

criteria.name: Structure & flow
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Judge FUNCTION, not template: does the opening frame the question, does the body progress logically, does the ending synthesise and look forward? Unconventional structures that do these things are not penalised.

bands.descriptor: No discernible organisation.
Loose organisation; no framing or ending.
Recognisable organisation; framing or synthesis weak.
Frames, progresses and concludes, with minor flow issues.
Opening frames the question; logical progression; ending synthesises and looks forward.

criteria.name: Presentation (handwritten)
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Handwritten answers only: diagrams, flowcharts, maps, headings, underlining and legibility. Never penalise handwriting style itself; only legibility that would hinder an examiner.

bands.descriptor: Largely illegible or unreadable layout.
Dense, hard-to-scan page.
Readable; no visual aids or headings.
Readable with headings or one useful visual.
Clear layout with purposeful visuals that add meaning.

criteria.name: Precision & language
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Clarity, concision and correct terminology. Weighted low. Never comment harshly on grammar; flag only what impairs meaning or wastes words. Word-limit status is computed by code.

bands.descriptor: Meaning frequently unclear.
Wordy or imprecise; meaning sometimes unclear.
Clear but wordy or loose with terms.
Clear and mostly concise; terms used correctly.
Crisp, precise and economical.
